description: A continuous risk management process is established, implemented, documented, and maintained across the AI system's lifecycle.
Training, validation, and testing data sets are subject to data governance practices covering relevance, representativeness, and error examination.
Technical documentation is drawn up before the system is placed on the market and kept up to date, demonstrating compliance with requirements.
The AI system is designed to allow automatic recording of events (logs) over the system's lifetime to ensure traceability.
The AI system is designed to be sufficiently transparent so deployers can interpret outputs and use the system appropriately.
The AI system is designed to be effectively overseen by natural persons, including the ability to intervene or halt the system.
The AI system achieves an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity, and performs consistently throughout its lifecycle.
A quality management system is in place ensuring compliance, including strategy for regulatory compliance and post-market monitoring.
The AI system undergoes the relevant conformity assessment procedure prior to being placed on the market or put into service.
A post-market monitoring system is established and proportionate to the nature of the AI technology and risks involved.
Processes exist to report serious incidents or malfunctioning to relevant market surveillance authorities within required timeframes.
